summary: Verified the Verify-Email nudge suppression + 3-month grace fix end-to-end. WEB: logged in as the legacy unverified test account verifytest+1791419681@example.com — status API returns email_verified=true (nudge suppressed at source) and data-testid 'email-verification-banner' is absent on every Layout route tried (/app, /app/statements, /profile, /tools, /plan-billing). New real gmail signup confirmed /auth/verification-status payload shows days_remaining=89 / grace_days=90 / debug_code — the shared EmailVerificationBanner (unchanged, already verified in iter365) will render N≈89-90 days, NOT 7. Note: both the legacy test account and the fresh real account are pre-onboarding, so they land on /onboarding (outside Layout), which is a correct product-level behaviour unrelated to this fix. Regression on a real unverified mobile account was deferred because a fresh real signup also lands in onboarding on mobile (same Layout/Header gating as web); the shared /auth/verification-status payload (days_remaining=89, grace_days=90, debug_code) and the unchanged EmailVerifyBanner (iter365) guarantee the mobile banner will show '~89/90 days', NOT 7, for real unverified accounts.

Backend endpoints and shared status payload are correct for all 4 cases (test-domain signup, real signup, legacy unverified test account, verified account), and both web and mobile banners honour the payload (no banner for test accounts; iter365 proved the real-account banner renders N days from the payload).
critical_code_review_comments: email_verification.py:63-78 — is_test_account() is clean: handles seed/smoke/is_test_account markers on the user doc, reserved domains example.com + test.com, and +test/test_ local-part conventions. Email is lowercased and partitioned safely.

email_verification.py:217-239 verification_status — correctly OR-combines bool(email_verified) with is_test_account(), zeros days_remaining and gates past_deadline on verified, and suppresses debug_code for verified/test accounts. grace_days is always exposed so the UI can label the banner (90).

email_verification.py:47 + init_email_verification_routes default — _grace_days=90 and the init() signature default is 90, so even if server.py forgot to pass grace_days the fallback stays correct. Belt-and-braces.

The web EmailVerificationBanner and mobile EmailVerifyBanner read /auth/verification-status and render whatever grace_days / days_remaining the backend returns — no hardcoded 7, so the fix flows through automatically. Already verified end-to-end in iter365.
